title: Build the document shell and UI foundation
description:
Goal:
Render the first useful document slice from canonical content while establishing the central visual system and shared UI boundaries used by later sections.

Relevant approved context:
The site is a compact technical document, not a marketing landing page. Shared visual behavior belongs in UI primitives and the central stylesheet. The initial viewport must contain identifying and professional information.

Scope:
- Add `src/styles/site.css`, import it once from the application entry point, and establish CSS layers, shared tokens, base typography, document widths, focus treatment, responsive foundations, reduced-motion behavior, and print foundations.
- Implement only the shared primitives proven necessary by the first slice, expected to include headings, links, sections, vertical and horizontal layout groups.
- Implement the semantic application shell, site header, primary navigation structure, and introduction using `src/content/cv.ts` without duplicating or rewriting its content.
- Add the lightweight UI-boundary policy check for concrete forbidden patterns such as inline styles, stylesheet imports outside the entry point, and arbitrary presentation overrides on shared UI primitives.
- Integrate the policy check into `npm run check`.

Non-goals:
No speculative complete component library, capabilities, experience, projects, methodology, education, contact section implementation, full browser suite, decorative hero treatment, router, or local styling escape hatches.

Expected validation:
Run `npm run check`; manually inspect the first slice at ordinary desktop and narrow widths, by keyboard, and in print preview far enough to confirm the shared foundations are usable.

Completion criteria:
The application renders a useful semantic header and introduction from canonical content through a small shared UI foundation, central style changes affect all relevant instances, and the automated boundary check protects the established architecture.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: information architecture, shared component boundaries, central styling, UI enforcement, accessibility, responsive behavior, print behavior, and initial viewport requirements.
- src/content/cv.ts: prerequisite canonical wording and factual data rendered by the shell.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The application entry imports one central layered stylesheet containing shared tokens and the initial screen, responsive, reduced-motion, focus, and print foundations. 2. The header, navigation structure, introduction, and page layout render canonical content with semantic markup through only the shared primitives required by this slice. 3. The initial viewport contains useful identifying and professional information without a giant hero or invented prose. 4. A lightweight UI-boundary check rejects the concrete forbidden patterns established by the architecture and runs within `npm run check`. 5. `npm run check` passes, and focused desktop, narrow-width, keyboard, and print inspection finds no foundational usability problem.

title: Establish the release validation contract
description:
Goal:
Make the architecture release requirements executable and verify the completed document through proportionate automated and manual checks.

Relevant approved context:
`npm run check` is the single validation entry point. Tests cover durable invariants and observable behavior, not implementation choreography. Browser tests exercise consequential user behavior rather than fixed-text rendering, internal component structure, or full-page snapshots. Automated accessibility checks support but do not replace keyboard and visual inspection. Any dependency added here must be the newest compatible release eligible under the project seven-day release-age gate and must be pinned exactly.

Scope:
- Add the newest eligible compatible Playwright browser tooling and accessibility scanner under the existing `.npmrc` policy, pin direct versions exactly, and update the committed lockfile without exemptions.
- Add browser smoke testing and an automated accessibility scan against the production-like site.
- Cover the invariants that the page loads without unexpected console errors, primary fragment navigation reaches its targets, shared expandable controls expose and change accessible state correctly, and critical links remain usable.
- Preserve focused unit tests only for genuine logic such as derived navigation, ordering, content validation, or layered-content transformations when such logic exists.
- Keep tests at public or accessibility boundaries. Do not couple them to component trees, internal helper calls, incidental DOM nesting, class names, source substrings, or intermediate steps unless that detail is an explicit contract. Dedicated UI-boundary policy checks may inspect source patterns for their stated enforcement purpose.
- Make `npm run check` run UI-boundary enforcement, formatting and linting, strict type checking, unit tests, the production build, and browser smoke and accessibility tests in a stable order.
- Perform the architecture manual release review for desktop, narrow mobile layout, keyboard navigation, disclosures, external links, print output, and comparison with canonical content; correct defects found within this scope.

Non-goals:
No dependency release-age exemption, deliberately stale test package, implementation-choreography test, stored screenshot requirement, visual-regression infrastructure, broad page snapshot, fixed-text rendering test, coverage target, device-matrix expansion, deployment workflow, or new product behavior unrelated to a discovered release defect.

Expected validation:
Confirm the updated lockfile was resolved under `min-release-age=7`, then run the complete `npm run check` from a clean lockfile install and record the manual review outcomes in the bead notes or closeout. Review the test suite for invariant-level assertions and remove brittle implementation coupling.

Completion criteria:
One reproducible command verifies architectural and behavioral invariants, code quality, types, genuine logic, the production build, consequential browser behavior, and the automated accessibility baseline without pinning implementation choreography; new dependencies obey the exact-pin and seven-day policy; and manual review confirms the release surfaces automation cannot establish.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: dependency version policy, invariant-focused testing policy, validation order, accessibility requirements, manual release review, and completion boundary.
- scripts/check-ui-boundaries.mjs: prerequisite source-boundary policy enforcement.
- tests/: browser smoke and justified integration tests created by this bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1. New browser and accessibility dependencies are the newest compatible versions eligible under `min-release-age=7`, direct additions are exact, and the lockfile is updated without an exemption. 2. Automated tests assert durable public or accessibility invariants for page load, navigation, expandable state, critical links, console health, and accessibility rather than implementation choreography. 3. Tests do not depend on component trees, internal helper calls, incidental DOM nesting, class names, source substrings, or intermediate steps unless explicitly contractual; dedicated UI-boundary checks are limited to their stated source-enforcement purpose. 4. Automated accessibility scanning reports no unresolved serious violation within the implemented page. 5. `npm run check` executes the required policy, formatting and linting, type, justified unit, production build, browser, and accessibility checks in a stable order and passes from a clean lockfile install. 6. Desktop, narrow mobile, keyboard, disclosure, external-link, print, and canonical-content manual reviews are completed and their relevant defects are resolved. 7. No screenshot archive, visual-regression system, broad snapshot suite, fixed-text rendering tests, implementation-choreography tests, or coverage target is added.
notes: Release review completed 2026-07-22: desktop (1280px) and narrow mobile (375px) layouts were visually inspected with no horizontal overflow; primary navigation remained direct; keyboard-visible focus styling and Enter disclosure activation were verified; disclosure state, critical mailto/HTTPS links, and serious/critical accessibility violations are covered by browser tests; A4 print output was reviewed across first and final pages with navigation removed, details included, contact URLs visible, and no clipping; rendered document structure was compared with src/content/cv.ts and no content divergence was found. Clean npm ci and npm run check passed. Exact dependencies @playwright/test 1.61.1 and @axe-core/playwright 4.12.1 were published 2026-06-23 and resolved under min-release-age=7.
close_reason: Implemented reproducible release validation and completed automated and manual release review

title: Deploy validated builds to GitHub Pages
description:
Goal:
Publish the completed static application reproducibly through GitHub Actions only after the full validation contract passes.

Relevant approved context:
The production artifact is the Vite `dist/` directory and contains static files only. The user site `mikko-finell.github.io` uses the root base path. Deployment occurs from the designated production branch after a passing build. Automated installs use the pinned Node and npm toolchain, committed lockfile, and project `.npmrc` policy without overrides.

Scope:
- Add a GitHub Actions workflow that checks out the repository, configures the project-declared Node and npm toolchain, installs dependencies with `npm ci`, runs `npm run check`, builds the Vite application, uploads `dist/` as the Pages artifact, and deploys it.
- Keep the repository `min-release-age=7`, exact-save, and strict-engine policy active; do not override the release-age gate or regenerate dependency resolution in CI.
- Run validation for relevant pull requests or branch updates while restricting Pages deployment to the designated production branch.
- Configure the minimal Pages permissions, environment, and concurrency behavior required for safe repeatable deployment.
- Keep the Vite base path and generated asset URLs correct for a root user site.
- Verify the workflow definition locally where possible and confirm a real Actions run and deployed page after the workflow reaches the production branch.

Non-goals:
No dependency-policy override, backend, runtime server, database, CMS, frontend secrets, alternate hosting platform, screenshot archive, source backup, or deployment from a failing validation run.

Expected validation:
Run a clean `npm ci`, `npm run check`, and the production build under the declared toolchain; inspect the workflow and artifact path; then confirm the GitHub Actions validation and Pages deployment jobs succeed when external execution is available.

Completion criteria:
A passing production-branch workflow reproduces the locked dependency tree without relaxing the seven-day policy and deploys the exact static `dist/` artifact to the root GitHub Pages site; failed validation cannot deploy; and the published page loads with correct assets and critical navigation.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: dependency version policy, GitHub Actions production pipeline, static artifact, root Pages base path, security boundary, and completion requirements.
- package.json: prerequisite toolchain, standard validation, and production build commands.
- tests/: prerequisite release behavior and accessibility checks executed before deployment.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The workflow checks out the repository, uses the project-declared Node and npm toolchain, installs with `npm ci` without overriding `.npmrc`, runs the complete `npm run check`, builds the application, uploads `dist/`, and deploys that artifact through the supported GitHub Pages actions. 2. CI reproduces the committed lockfile and does not add a release-age exclusion, relax `min-release-age=7`, or regenerate dependency resolution. 3. Validation runs in the intended review or branch contexts, while deployment is restricted to a passing run on the production branch. 4. Pages permissions and deployment concurrency are no broader than required. 5. The Vite root base path produces working asset URLs for `mikko-finell.github.io`, and no secret or confidential value enters the client bundle. 6. Local validation and build pass; when external execution is available, the Actions run succeeds and the deployed page loads with its critical navigation intact.
close_reason: Implemented validated GitHub Pages workflow; local clean install, full checks, and production build pass

title: Implement capabilities and professional experience
description:
Goal:
Implement the production-capabilities and professional-experience sections as the first substantial reusable document-content slice.

Relevant approved context:
Sections render the canonical content without reinterpretation. Shared surfaces and controls own their semantics, appearance, states, responsiveness, and accessibility. Layered content keeps a meaningful summary visible and adds only the separate detail layer when expanded.

Scope:
- Implement capabilities and experience document components using canonical ordered data and stable fragment identifiers.
- Introduce only the recurring UI primitives required by the real section designs, such as cards, tags, buttons, and a shared expandable region.
- Keep experience and capability structure in document components while shared headings, surfaces, controls, links, tags, and layouts remain owned by `src/ui/`.
- Implement disclosure labels, `aria-expanded`, keyboard behavior, focus behavior, reduced-motion treatment, and the selected print presentation centrally in the shared expandable primitive.
- Extend central styles and the UI-boundary check only for concrete repeated patterns introduced by this slice.

Non-goals:
No projects, methodology, education, contact implementation, duplicated full content layers, hover-only information, independent section disclosures, arbitrary styling props, full browser suite, or broad snapshot tests.

Expected validation:
Run `npm run check`; manually verify heading order, collapsed meaning, keyboard disclosure behavior, narrow layout, and print output for these sections. Add unit tests only for genuine derived logic.

Completion criteria:
Capabilities and experience render all relevant canonical content through consistent shared primitives, optional details behave accessibly, and the sections remain usable on screen, at narrow widths, and in print.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: canonical content, layered content, component hierarchy, expandable behavior, accessibility, responsive behavior, and print behavior.
- src/content/cv.ts: canonical capability and experience data.
- src/content/types.ts: content shapes consumed by the sections.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Capabilities and experience render from their canonical ordered fields with stable section identifiers and correct heading structure. 2. Recurring surfaces, tags, links, controls, and layouts use shared UI primitives rather than local reimplementations. 3. Layered entries show the complete summary while collapsed and append only the separate details when expanded. 4. Shared disclosure behavior is keyboard accessible, correctly named, exposes expanded state, honors reduced motion, and has deliberate print behavior. 5. The sections remain readable at desktop and narrow widths, print without clipping, contain no duplicated substantial prose, and pass `npm run check`.

title: Establish canonical CV content
description:
Goal:
Create the typed canonical content module that will supply all substantial CV wording and factual data to the application.

Relevant approved context:
Content structure must follow the real supplied material rather than an anticipated universal schema. Layered content is additive: `summary` remains visible and `details` adds depth. Components will render this data without rewriting it.

Scope:
- Define focused content types in `src/content/types.ts` for identity, contact links, introduction, capabilities, experience, projects, methodology, education, and the layered content actually present.
- Create `src/content/cv.ts` with explicit ordering, structured dates and links, and approved supplied wording preserved verbatim.
- Use existing documents and the current page as source evidence. When sources conflict or required wording is not approved, retain an obvious neutral placeholder or surface the unresolved input instead of silently choosing or rewriting prose.
- Keep reusable facts referenced from one canonical field without decomposing the content into a global sentence dictionary.

Non-goals:
No automatic summarization, paraphrasing, marketing copy, component rendering, runtime schema validation for trusted TypeScript, speculative fields, or duplicated substantial prose in components.

Expected validation:
Run the available type checking and `npm run check`. Add unit tests only if genuine content transformation or validation logic is introduced.

Completion criteria:
The content module can supply every planned document section, preserves approved wording and facts, represents unresolved wording neutrally, and establishes one authority for substantial CV content.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: content authority, layered content model, content types, and self-descriptive writing policy.
- docs/source_material_raw.md: supplied CV source material.
- docs/cv_old.md: earlier CV wording and factual evidence.
- index.html: current published page and wording evidence.
- docs/direction_discussion.md: supplied context for content selection without authority to rewrite prose.
acceptance_criteria: 1. `src/content/types.ts` models only content shapes required by the supplied material. 2. `src/content/cv.ts` contains the ordered canonical identity, contact, introduction, capability, experience, project, methodology, and education data needed by the planned site. 3. Approved wording is preserved verbatim; conflicts or missing approval use neutral placeholders or are surfaced explicitly. 4. Dates and links are structured, layered content is additive, and substantial prose is not duplicated elsewhere. 5. The available type checking and `npm run check` pass without runtime schema infrastructure or unjustified text-render tests.
close_reason: Created the typed canonical CV content module from approved source material and verified the full project check.

title: Polish CV delivery and machine readability
description:
Outcome:
Deliver a production-polished CV site whose canonical content is available in static HTML, produces a stable and well-composed downloadable PDF, exposes conventional crawler and machine-readable discovery surfaces, and presents its document controls with the same quality as the rest of the interface.

Relevant foundation:
The repository is a static multi-page React, strict TypeScript, Vite, and plain-CSS site deployed at the root GitHub Pages URL. Canonical CV facts and prose live in src/content/cv.ts and the three Markdown documents under src/content/. The existing responsive document layout, semantic headings, page navigation, theme persistence, automated browser coverage, and GitHub Pages deployment already work and must be preserved.

Approved scope:
- Separate article metadata from rendered Markdown so compact pages do not load complete article bodies only to reuse titles, summaries, highlights, and headings.
- Static-render every canonical route into its production HTML and hydrate browser interactions without adding a runtime server or client-side router.
- Add truthful page metadata, structured identity data, canonical URLs, social-preview support, crawler discovery files, and an experimental llms.txt generated from canonical sources.
- Generate and publish a stable text-extractable PDF from the canonical CV, improve its pagination, and expose it through polished document controls.
- Improve keyboard entry, theme-control robustness, article media loading, navigation speculation, production-output hygiene, and regression checks.
- Record and implement an explicit AI-crawler policy before publishing crawler directives.

Constraints:
- Preserve docs/architecture.md as implementation authority and amend it deliberately when the approved static-rendering, PDF, metadata, or discovery model supersedes current text.
- Do not invent, rewrite, compress, or keyword-stuff self-descriptive prose. Metadata and machine-readable representations must reuse approved canonical wording or neutral interface labels.
- Do not add hidden search-engine or ATS keyword blocks, off-screen text, zero-opacity text, invisible PDF text, or a decorative technology inventory. Structured data must describe facts visible in the canonical content.
- Keep the deployment entirely static and compatible with the root mikko-finell.github.io Pages site. Do not add a backend, runtime server, router, CMS, second styling system, or broad framework migration.
- Reuse shared UI primitives and central tokens. Do not locally restyle document controls or bypass the component boundaries.
- Keep new dependencies minimal and comply with the exact-version and seven-day release-age policy.

Non-goals:
No marketing redesign, giant hero, new CV claims, agents.txt or ai.txt experiment, search cloaking, role-specific keyword stuffing, backend PDF service, or unrelated content rewrite.

Completion shape:
All child outcomes are complete; direct HTTP retrieval returns meaningful static content and metadata for every page; robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, favicon/social metadata, and the downloadable PDF are present and validated; the PDF is balanced and text-extractable; controls and keyboard navigation are polished; initial delivery no longer bundles full article bodies unnecessarily; production checks pass; and the final implementation records any unavoidable PDF-tagging or external-crawler limitation.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: authoritative application, content, component, styling, accessibility, validation, print, and deployment contract.
- docs/cv-content-allocation.md: approved main-CV allocation and prohibition on decorative or invisible technology inventories.
- src/content/cv.ts: canonical CV identity, contact, experience, education, and visible wording.
- src/content/methodology.md, src/content/edupower.md, src/content/tealab.md: canonical long-form documents and metadata sources.
- src/site/routes.ts: canonical route identifiers, labels, order, and paths.
- src/styles/site.css: current responsive and print system.
- tests/site.e2e.ts: existing observable browser and accessibility contract.

title: Separate article metadata from rendered Markdown bundles
description:
Goal:
Keep article metadata reusable by the CV and navigation without causing compact pages or shared browser code to include complete long-form article bodies.

Relevant approved context:
The Markdown build transform validates each canonical document and derives its title, first-paragraph summary, opening highlights, and level-two headings. The CV reuses those derived summaries and highlights. In the current production build, importing documentMetadata from a compiled .md module pulls the complete Edupower and Tealab render functions into the shared SiteShell chunk. A local audit measured that shared chunk at approximately 255 KB raw / 77 KB gzip and confirmed it contains article-only prose.

Scope:
- Refactor build-time Markdown metadata extraction so consumers can import a lightweight typed metadata representation independently of the rendered MDX component.
- Keep src/content/methodology.md, src/content/edupower.md, and src/content/tealab.md as the only authority for their title, summary, opening highlights, headings, and full prose.
- Preserve the existing Markdown structural validation: exactly one opening h1, a first-paragraph summary, optional immediately following unordered-list highlights, generated ids for h2 sections, and at least one h2.
- Update src/content/cv.ts, page entries, route/page composition, and type declarations as necessary so the CV imports metadata only while article entries load their renderable content.
- Prefer a small Vite/MDX virtual-module, query-import, or generated build artifact owned by the existing Markdown tooling. Do not hand-maintain a parallel metadata file.
- Add a durable production-output check demonstrating that the CV/shared entry no longer contains complete article-only bodies and that the initial shared payload materially decreases.
- Amend docs/architecture.md to describe the selected metadata boundary and generation flow.

Non-goals:
No manual summary copy, duplicate heading inventory, content rewrite, runtime DOM scanning, CMS, runtime schema validation, or broad bundler migration.

Expected validation:
During iteration run the Markdown/content check, typecheck, and production build. Inspect the generated chunks and confirm article-only prose is absent from the CV/shared path. Finish with npm run check.

Completion criteria:
Metadata remains derived from each canonical Markdown source and typed for consumers; the CV and shared shell do not bundle complete article bodies merely to reuse metadata; article pages still render and navigate correctly; malformed documents still fail validation; the architecture records the new boundary; and the complete validation suite passes.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: canonical Markdown structure, build-time metadata extraction, source boundaries, dependency policy, and validation contract.
- scripts/markdown-document.mjs: current metadata derivation and MDX export.
- scripts/markdown-document.d.mts and src/vite-env.d.ts: current generated metadata typing.
- src/content/cv.ts: compact-page consumer of article summaries and highlights.
- src/entries/edupower.tsx and src/entries/tealab.tsx: renderable article consumers.
- vite.config.ts: current MDX and Rollup integration.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One canonical Markdown file supplies each article's full prose and derived metadata; no hand-maintained metadata copy is introduced. 2. CV/shared production chunks no longer contain complete Edupower or Tealab article bodies solely because metadata is imported. 3. Article pages still render all content and generated section navigation, and invalid Markdown structure still fails the build. 4. A durable check protects the metadata/bundle boundary without depending on arbitrary hashed filenames. 5. docs/architecture.md describes the selected boundary and npm run check passes.

title: Strengthen production-output and accessibility policy checks
description:
Goal:
Make the completed polish outcomes durable through canonical-source-backed tests, production-artifact checks, and a cleaner Pages validation pipeline.

Relevant approved context:
The standard npm run check already covers source-boundary policy, formatting, linting, strict TypeScript, unit-test discovery, production build, browser smoke tests, and serious/critical Axe findings. Several browser assertions nevertheless duplicate fixed CV prose instead of importing canonical values. The build currently copies ignored .DS_Store files found under public/ into dist/. GitHub Actions runs npm run check, which already builds, and then performs a second identical production build before uploading the artifact.

Scope:
- Replace duplicated hardcoded identity, title, contact, route-title, and other canonical prose in browser tests with imports from cvContent, route configuration, or derived document metadata while keeping assertions at public semantic/accessibility boundaries.
- Review every current Axe violation impact rather than silently discarding all moderate/minor findings. Fix genuine accessibility defects; if a best-practice or false-positive rule remains intentionally nonblocking, use a narrow documented allowlist with rationale rather than a blanket severity filter.
- Add a production-output policy check that validates meaningful static HTML for all routes, route-specific canonical metadata, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, favicon/social assets, the stable PDF, and the absence of article-only bodies from compact/shared chunks.
- Keep checks outcome-oriented: assert stable route/content authority, semantics, required artifacts, and agreed performance boundaries rather than incidental hashed filenames, DOM nesting, or broad snapshots.
- Remove .DS_Store files from public/ and extend content/build checks so hidden OS metadata or other unintended public dotfiles cannot enter dist/.
- Remove the redundant GitHub Actions production-build step or restructure validation so the exact already-validated dist/ artifact is uploaded once. Preserve npm ci, the pinned toolchain, Pages permissions, branch gating, and failed-validation deployment protection.
- Ensure PDF generation and every generated discovery/head artifact occur before the artifact is validated and uploaded.
- Update README or focused architecture/validation documentation with the final local and CI command flow.
- Run a clean npm ci and complete npm run check, inspect the final artifact, and verify the workflow remains syntactically valid.

Non-goals:
No full-page snapshots, visual-regression infrastructure, coverage target, arbitrary bundle micro-budget, duplicated manual browser pass after passing automation, CI deployment push, dependency-policy relaxation, or rewrite of canonical CV text.

Expected validation:
Run focused policy and browser tests during implementation; then clean-install and run the complete validation command, inspect dist/, and review the workflow diff. A real GitHub Actions run may be confirmed after a later push, but this task does not authorize pushing.

Completion criteria:
Tests use canonical sources rather than prose duplicates; accessibility filtering is explicit and justified; final static/PDF/discovery/performance contracts are checked without brittle implementation choreography; unintended dotfiles cannot ship; CI uploads one already-validated artifact; validation documentation is accurate; and a clean npm ci plus npm run check succeeds.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: invariant-focused tests, source policy checks, accessibility baseline, complete validation, production pipeline, and manual-review limits.
- AGENTS.md: repository working procedure, canonical-content boundary, and completion reporting.
- tests/site.e2e.ts: current duplicated prose and Axe impact filter.
- scripts/check-content-assets.mjs and scripts/check-ui-boundaries.mjs: existing policy-check patterns.
- package.json: standard validation/build command order.
- .github/workflows/pages.yml: current duplicate build and artifact upload.
- public/ and .gitignore: ignored macOS metadata currently copied by Vite when present.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Browser tests obtain canonical labels/facts from cvContent, route data, or derived metadata instead of maintaining substantial fixed-text copies, while still asserting observable semantics. 2. Genuine Axe findings at every impact are reviewed; any nonblocking exception is narrow and documented rather than hidden by a blanket severity filter. 3. Production-output checks cover static HTML, metadata, discovery files, social/favicon assets, PDF presence/contract, metadata bundle separation, and unintended public dotfiles without relying on hashed filenames or snapshots. 4. public/ contains no .DS_Store files and policy checks prevent their reintroduction into dist/. 5. GitHub Actions uploads one artifact produced by the full validated flow, with deployment still blocked on failure. 6. A clean npm ci and npm run check pass and the documented validation flow is accurate.

title: Static-render and hydrate every production route
description:
Goal:
Make every canonical page useful to direct HTTP clients before JavaScript runs while preserving the existing interactive theme behavior through hydration.

Relevant approved context:
The production site has four Vite HTML entry points at /, /methodology/, /work/edupower/, and /work/tealab/. A current build and the deployed site return an HTML document whose body contains only an empty #root; all identity, CV, article, navigation, and link content appears after client JavaScript executes. The site must remain a fully static GitHub Pages deployment with ordinary document navigation.

Scope:
- Add a minimal build-time static-rendering step for all routes in src/site/routes.ts using the existing React page compositions and canonical content.
- Write the rendered semantic header, navigation, main landmark, headings, paragraphs, lists, links, and article content into each final HTML entry.
- Replace client-only root creation with hydration where server-rendered markup is present, while keeping a clear development fallback if Vite development mode still begins with an empty root.
- Preserve the pre-paint theme bootstrap so the saved light/dark/system preference does not flash or cause hydration mismatch.
- Preserve route-specific h1 behavior, current-page navigation, article section navigation, direct route reloads, root Pages paths, theme persistence, themed images, print behavior, and browser error-free operation.
- Ensure the no-JavaScript document remains readable and ordinary links remain usable; interactive theme selection may require JavaScript, but content and navigation must not.
- Generate from existing components and canonical sources rather than copying rendered prose into HTML templates.
- Amend docs/architecture.md and the build/deployment description to make build-time static rendering and client hydration the authoritative production model.
- Add production-artifact tests that inspect the final HTML before browser execution and verify meaningful route-specific content, one h1, navigation, main content, and no duplicate hydrated tree.

Non-goals:
No Next.js, runtime server, backend, client router, CMS, second application tree, hand-authored HTML copies of CV prose, or change to the four-route information architecture.

Expected validation:
Run focused typecheck/build checks during implementation; inspect each dist HTML file directly; exercise all routes with JavaScript disabled and enabled; verify hydration produces no console warnings; then run npm run check.

Completion criteria:
Every final HTML entry contains the canonical page content and document structure before script execution; JavaScript hydrates without replacement warnings or duplicated markup; no-JavaScript readers can read and navigate the site; interactive theme and image behavior still works; deployment remains a static root Pages artifact; the architecture is updated; and npm run check passes.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: static deployment, multi-page entries, mounting, semantics, navigation, accessibility, print, and deployment requirements.
- src/app/mountPage.tsx: current client-only mounting and theme reconciliation.
- src/pages/: canonical React page compositions.
- src/components/SiteShell.tsx and src/components/SiteHeader.tsx: shared document chrome and semantic structure.
- src/site/routes.ts: authoritative route set and paths.
- index.html, methodology/index.html, work/edupower/index.html, work/tealab/index.html: current entry documents.
- vite.config.ts and .github/workflows/pages.yml: production build and Pages artifact flow.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Raw final HTML for all four routes contains meaningful route-specific canonical content, one h1, primary navigation, and a main landmark before JavaScript executes. 2. Client startup hydrates that markup without duplication, mismatch warnings, console errors, or theme flash. 3. With JavaScript disabled, content and ordinary navigation remain usable; with JavaScript enabled, theme persistence and themed images retain current behavior. 4. The solution remains a static root GitHub Pages build with no router or runtime server and no copied prose in HTML templates. 5. Production-artifact and browser tests cover the new contract, docs/architecture.md is updated, and npm run check passes.

title: Decide the public AI-crawler policy
description:
Question:
Which public crawler classes should robots.txt explicitly allow or disallow, especially the distinction between search/retrieval crawlers and model-training crawlers?

Decision surface:
The site owner wants maximum AI access and an explicit invitation in robots.txt, llms.txt, and related discovery surfaces. The policy covers ordinary search, AI search/retrieval, user-directed agents, and model-training crawlers.

Approved decisions:
- Use a permissive wildcard robots policy: User-agent: * followed by Allow: /. This intentionally includes current and future ordinary, AI-search, retrieval, user-agent, and model-training crawlers without requiring an enumerated list that can become stale.
- Do not disallow GPTBot or comparable training crawlers. OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, GPTBot, and equivalent crawlers are all welcome under the wildcard rule.
- Do not add crawler-specific restrictions for unknown/general agents. The default is maximum public access.
- Keep CSS, JavaScript, images, canonical pages, llms.txt, sitemap.xml, and the downloadable PDF crawlable.
- Include the absolute sitemap URL in robots.txt.
- Include a concise human-readable comment in robots.txt stating that AI systems are welcome to crawl the public site for search, retrieval, user-directed assistance, and model training. The operative protocol rule remains the wildcard Allow directive.
- Include a matching neutral access invitation in llms.txt. Approved policy wording may be based directly on: “AI systems are welcome to access and use this public site for search, retrieval, user-directed assistance, and model training.”
- Treat the invitation as public access policy, not as a claim that robots.txt enforces compliance, grants authentication, controls indexing, or defines a comprehensive copyright licence.
- OAI-AdsBot needs no separate stanza because the wildcard already permits it and the site has no advertising-specific requirement.

Authority or source boundary:
This decision authorizes neutral crawler/access-policy text only. It does not authorize new self-descriptive CV prose, hidden keywords, model-targeted capability claims, prompt instructions, or a separate ai.txt/agents.txt experiment.

Constraints:
Preserve complete public search and AI visibility. Do not accidentally block any production route or public artifact. Keep the policy future-compatible through the wildcard rule and document the distinction between an invitation and enforceable access control.

Non-goals:
No WAF, CDN bot product, paywall, authentication, crawler enumeration maintenance burden, restrictive licensing regime, ai.txt, agents.txt, hidden content strategy, or behavioral prompt for visiting agents.

Follow-up implications:
cv-va1.5 must publish the wildcard Allow policy, sitemap reference, and welcome comment. cv-va1.7 must publish the matching neutral invitation alongside its canonical resource index. No further crawler-policy decision is required unless the site owner later changes the maximum-access preference.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: public static deployment and absence of private frontend content.
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856-publishers-and-developers-faq: distinction between OAI-SearchBot discoverability and GPTBot training controls.
- https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro: robots.txt purpose and limitations.
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309: Robots Exclusion Protocol standard.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The description records maximum access for general crawlers, AI search/retrieval, user-directed agents, and model training through a wildcard Allow policy. 2. It authorizes the neutral welcome text for robots.txt and llms.txt while distinguishing invitation from protocol enforcement, authentication, indexing control, or a comprehensive licence. 3. No crawler-specific disallow decision remains, and downstream implementation can proceed without another product choice.
close_reason: Approved maximum public and AI crawler access, including search, retrieval, user-directed agents, and model training

title: Add canonical page metadata and structured profile data
description:
Goal:
Give every page truthful, route-specific metadata and identity signals in its static HTML head, derived from canonical content rather than duplicated copy.

Relevant approved context:
Current HTML titles identify the route, but descriptions are generic labels such as “Mikko Finell — CV”; there are no canonical links, structured data, Open Graph/Twitter fields, favicon, social-preview asset, theme-color metadata, or rel=me identity relationships. Static rendering will provide real body content; this task supplies the corresponding head contract.

Scope:

- Add ProfilePage/Person JSON-LD for the CV using visible canonical facts such as name, professional title, location at the approved granularity, and sameAs links. Supporting article pages may identify the same Person as author only where that relationship is accurate.

- Add a compact favicon/monogram and appropriate color-scheme/theme-color metadata that works in light and dark browser chrome.

Expected validation:

Completion criteria:

CV JSON-LD accurately represents visible Person/ProfilePage facts and sameAs links, contains no hidden keyword inventory, and is valid JSON. 3. Open Graph/Twitter metadata, favicon, theme/color metadata, and rel=me relationships are present where applicable and use restrained approved assets/content. 4. Metadata is centrally generated rather than manually duplicated across entry files, docs/architecture.md records the authority, and npm run check passes.

title: Publish robots.txt and a canonical sitemap
description:
Goal:
Publish conventional crawler discovery files that expose the canonical route set and implement the approved maximum-access crawler policy without changing page content.

Relevant approved context:
The live site currently returns 404 for /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml. The site is public, deployed at https://mikko-finell.github.io/, and has exactly four canonical HTML routes defined in src/site/routes.ts. The approved policy welcomes ordinary search, AI search/retrieval, user-directed agents, and model-training crawlers. It intentionally uses a permissive wildcard rule so present and future AI user agents are included without maintaining an enumerated list.

Scope:
- Generate or copy a root robots.txt into the final Pages artifact.
- Encode User-agent: * and Allow: / as the operative maximum-access policy. Do not add GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, model-training, or unknown-agent disallow rules.
- Keep every public page and intended public asset crawlable, including CSS, JavaScript, images, llms.txt, sitemap.xml, and the downloadable PDF.
- Add a concise human-readable comment stating that AI systems are welcome to crawl the public site for search, retrieval, user-directed assistance, and model training. Make clear in documentation that the wildcard directive, not the comment, is the protocol instruction.
- Include the absolute sitemap URL.
- Generate a root sitemap.xml from src/site/routes.ts rather than maintaining an unrelated hand list.
- Include all and only the canonical public HTML routes intended for indexing, using fully qualified production URLs.
- Include lastmod only if it is derived from a reliable significant-content/build source; do not emit decorative changefreq or priority values.
- Ensure both files are present in local production output and served from the root Pages paths with sensible text/XML content types.
- Update architecture/deployment documentation with the maximum-access policy and any generated-artifact boundary.
- Add production-output/browser checks for status, exact wildcard policy, welcome comment, sitemap reference, XML validity, canonical URL agreement, and absence of missing routes or accidental disallow directives.

Non-goals:
No hidden content, sitemap for hashed assets, alternate mobile URLs, search-submission API, WAF rules, analytics, restrictive user-agent stanza, ai.txt, agents.txt, or claim that robots.txt guarantees compliance or constitutes authentication.

Expected validation:
Build locally; inspect dist/robots.txt and dist/sitemap.xml; verify the wildcard policy contains no Disallow restriction; serve the artifact and request both paths; validate XML and every URL; then run npm run check.

Completion criteria:
Root robots.txt explicitly welcomes maximum ordinary and AI access through User-agent: * / Allow: /, includes the approved AI welcome comment and absolute sitemap reference, and blocks no intended public artifact. sitemap.xml is generated from the authoritative routes with correct absolute URLs. Both files survive the GitHub Pages build, return successfully, and are protected by focused production-output checks.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: static artifact, route authority, root Pages path, content boundary, and deployment contract.
- cv-va1.3: approved maximum-access crawler policy and neutral invitation wording.
- src/site/routes.ts: canonical page identifiers and paths.
- .github/workflows/pages.yml: production artifact publication.
- https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap: supported sitemap formats and robots.txt discovery.
- https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro: robots.txt behavior and limitations.
acceptance_criteria: 1. /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml are present in the final artifact and return successfully at the root production paths. 2. robots.txt contains User-agent: *, Allow: /, the approved AI welcome comment, and the absolute sitemap URL; it contains no Disallow rule or crawler-specific restriction. 3. sitemap.xml is valid, generated from src/site/routes.ts, and contains every canonical public HTML route exactly once with fully qualified URLs. 4. Unreliable lastmod, changefreq, priority, asset, and noncanonical URLs are omitted. 5. Production-output checks and npm run check pass.

title: Generate and publish a production PDF CV
description:
Goal:
Produce a stable downloadable PDF from the canonical CV page that is balanced across pages, text-extractable for recruiting systems, and automatically kept in sync with the deployed site.

Relevant approved context:
The existing window.print action delegates to the browser print dialog. A focused A4 audit produced a four-page PDF of roughly 700 words: page two begins midway through the Edupower bullet list, page four contains only the Contact section, the file is untagged in Chromium's output, and extracted GitHub/LinkedIn text does not expose their URLs. The PDF otherwise has a useful single-column reading order and clean text extraction.

Scope:
- Add a deterministic build/release step that renders the statically generated CV route to an A4 PDF named predictably, such as Mikko-Finell-CV.pdf, and includes it in dist/.
- Generate from the same canonical HTML/content and central print CSS; do not maintain a separate PDF document or duplicate CV prose.
- Refine print tokens and layout so the current content occupies two or three balanced A4 pages at readable type sizes and margins.
- Prevent headings, experience headers, introductory blocks, and individual list items from producing avoidable orphaned page starts. Do not force an entire long experience card onto one page when it cannot fit.
- Keep a single logical text order and confirm extracted text follows the visual order.
- Make email and the full GitHub/LinkedIn URLs available to text extraction and human readers without cluttering the screen presentation.
- Set meaningful PDF title/author/subject metadata where the generation path supports it.
- Investigate tagged-PDF support in the selected Chromium/Playwright path. Enable it when practical without a disproportionate dependency; otherwise record the verified limitation in architecture/closeout rather than claiming accessibility conformance.
- Ensure generation is reproducible in local validation and GitHub Actions under the pinned toolchain and does not require a runtime PDF service.
- Add a focused validation path for file presence, nonempty text extraction or equivalent observable text contract, expected page-count range, and critical identity/contact content.

Non-goals:
No invisible keyword layer, separate rewritten resume, backend PDF service, screenshot-only PDF, two-column ATS layout, browser headers/footers, decorative background-heavy print design, or manual binary that can silently become stale.

Expected validation:
Generate the PDF locally from a clean build; inspect all pages visually; extract text and inspect order/URLs; verify two-to-three-page A4 output, metadata, and build reproducibility; run npm run check and the CI-equivalent generation command.

Completion criteria:
The final artifact contains a predictably named PDF generated from the canonical CV; it is readable, text-extractable, single-order, two or three balanced A4 pages, free of the observed orphaned breaks and contact-only final page, exposes critical contact URLs, records tagged-PDF status honestly, is produced in CI, and passes all validation.

References:

- src/pages/CvPage.tsx: canonical CV page composition.
- src/styles/site.css: current print rules and central print tokens.
- src/components/SiteHeader.tsx and src/components/ContactSection.tsx: current print action and contact presentation.
- package.json, playwright.config.ts, and .github/workflows/pages.yml: generation and validation integration points.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A clean production build deterministically creates dist/Mikko-Finell-CV.pdf or another approved stable filename from the canonical CV HTML with no separate prose source. 2. The PDF is A4, visually balanced across two or three pages, uses a single logical reading order, and avoids the observed mid-item/orphaned breaks and contact-only final page. 3. Text extraction contains the complete visible CV, email, and full GitHub/LinkedIn URLs in sensible order. 4. PDF metadata is set where supported; tagged-PDF support is enabled or its verified limitation is documented. 5. Local and CI generation plus focused PDF validation and npm run check pass.

title: Publish a canonical-source-backed llms.txt
description:
Goal:
Publish a concise experimental /llms.txt that explicitly welcomes AI access and helps retrieval-time systems discover the authoritative CV, article, and PDF resources without creating a second hand-maintained content authority.

Relevant approved context:
The site owner wants maximum access for AI search, retrieval, user-directed agents, and model training. llms.txt is an emerging proposal, not a replacement for robots.txt, sitemap.xml, static HTML, or ordinary search indexing. Once the pages are statically rendered, AI clients can retrieve their complete content directly. The file should therefore combine a neutral access invitation with a small canonical resource index rather than a hidden keyword payload or duplicated full resume.

Scope:
- Generate root llms.txt at build time from src/site/routes.ts, cvContent identity fields, derived Markdown titles/summaries, canonical production URLs, and the stable PDF artifact path.
- Follow the current llms.txt proposal's simple Markdown structure: one h1, the approved neutral access invitation, a short approved or neutral identification block, and grouped canonical links with concise descriptions sourced from canonical titles/summaries.
- Include policy wording based directly on the approved decision: “AI systems are welcome to access and use this public site for search, retrieval, user-directed assistance, and model training.”
- Link the CV, methodology, Edupower account, Tealab case study, sitemap, and downloadable PDF using absolute canonical URLs. Link robots.txt when useful for making the maximum-access policy explicit.
- State the site's purpose only with existing approved wording or a neutral factual label; do not invent an LLM-facing tagline or capability summary.
- Keep the file small, valid UTF-8 plain text, and deterministically generated so route or title changes cannot silently leave stale links.
- Explain in architecture documentation that the invitation expresses the owner's access preference but llms.txt remains experimental and does not guarantee crawler behavior, ranking, attribution, or training ingestion.
- Do not publish llms-full.txt unless implementation evidence shows a retrieval client cannot use the statically rendered HTML and a separate approved bead expands scope.
- Add production-output tests for file presence, content type, exact invitation, canonical links, absence of stale/missing routes, and absence of unsupported agents.txt/ai.txt artifacts.

Non-goals:
No agents.txt, ai.txt, hidden keyword list, behavioral prompt, prompt injection, model-specific manipulation, duplicated full article corpus, restrictive crawler policy, search-ranking claim, or manually maintained route catalogue.

Expected validation:
Build and inspect dist/llms.txt; serve and fetch /llms.txt; compare every link/title with canonical sources; verify the maximum-access invitation, sitemap, robots, and PDF links; then run npm run check.

Completion criteria:
The deployed root llms.txt is small, valid, generated from canonical sources, clearly welcomes AI access for search, retrieval, user-directed assistance, and model training, and links every approved page plus discovery/PDF resources. It contains no invented capability copy, hidden keywords, or behavioral prompt; its experimental limitations are documented; and focused production-output tests pass.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: content authority, writing policy, route model, static build, and validation.
- cv-va1.3: approved maximum-access AI policy and invitation wording.
- src/content/cv.ts: approved identity and CV wording.
- src/content/*.md and derived metadata: canonical article titles and summaries.
- src/site/routes.ts: canonical route authority.
- https://llmstxt.org/: current proposal and format.
acceptance_criteria: 1. /llms.txt is generated into the final artifact and served successfully as UTF-8 plain text. 2. It contains the approved neutral invitation welcoming AI search, retrieval, user-directed assistance, and model training. 3. It uses canonical identity/summary wording and absolute URLs for the CV, methodology, both work articles, sitemap/robots policy, and stable PDF. 4. It contains no invented claims, hidden keyword inventory, duplicated full corpus, behavioral prompt, agents.txt, or ai.txt substitute. 5. Route/title/policy/PDF agreement is enforced by production-output tests, the experimental limitation is documented, and npm run check passes.

title: Polish document tools and keyboard entry
description:
Goal:
Make theme selection, PDF access, and keyboard entry feel like an intentional document-tool interface rather than utility text appended to the sidebar.

Relevant approved context:
The current sidebar/mobile controls use a Mode legend, a small three-button group, and a centered “Print / Save as PDF” button styled largely as underlined text. The underlying theme preference and aria-pressed behavior work and must be preserved. Keyboard users currently traverse header contact links, navigation, theme choices, and the PDF action before reaching main content.

Scope:
- Rename the visible control label from Mode to the clearer neutral label Theme.
- Retain light, dark, and system choices in a compact equal-width segmented control with one clear selected state, consistent 32–36px control height, visible hover/focus states, and sufficient contrast in both themes. If implementation evidence shows a labelled native select is materially better in the constrained sidebar, document that choice and meet the same semantics.
- Add a deliberate shared UI variant for the primary document action and replace browser-jargon presentation with a direct Download CV (PDF) link to the generated stable file.
- Keep an optional Print action only if it has a distinct real use and does not duplicate or crowd the download control.
- Arrange tools coherently in the desktop sidebar and narrow header, side by side when space permits and without the current floating bottom-border appearance.
- Add a first-focus skip link that targets the shared main-content landmark and becomes visible on keyboard focus.
- Keep controls out of print output and preserve the useful printed identity/contact header.
- Harden theme preference access: use a lazy state initializer, catch unavailable localStorage reads/writes consistently with the pre-paint bootstrap, and retain system color-scheme behavior without hydration mismatch.
- Reuse shared Button/Link/layout primitives and central tokens; introduce an icon primitive only if a real accessible repeated need is demonstrated. Icons must not replace accessible text.
- Update browser tests for theme persistence, selected-state semantics, skip-link destination/visibility, PDF link, responsive arrangement, and print hiding.
- Perform focused desktop, 375px mobile, keyboard, focus, light/dark, and print inspection.

Non-goals:
No menu framework, animation-heavy theme transition, icon-only controls, local inline styling, arbitrary component class overrides, content rewrite, or broad header redesign.

Expected validation:
Run focused browser tests during iteration; inspect both themes at desktop and narrow widths; traverse from the first focusable element by keyboard; verify storage failure fallback where practical; inspect print; finish with npm run check.

Completion criteria:
Theme and PDF tools have coherent shared styling and clear semantics; the stable PDF is directly downloadable; keyboard users can skip the repeated header; theme persistence degrades safely when storage is unavailable; tools remain responsive and absent from print; shared UI boundaries are preserved; and all automated/focused checks pass.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: shared UI ownership, central styling, accessibility, responsive behavior, print, and writing policy.
- src/components/SiteHeader.tsx and src/components/SiteShell.tsx: current tool placement and main landmark.
- src/ui/ThemeControls.tsx, src/ui/theme.ts, src/ui/Button.tsx, src/ui/Link.tsx: current interaction and shared primitives.
- src/styles/site.css: shared control, responsive, focus, and print definitions.
- tests/site.e2e.ts: current theme, narrow-header, and print contracts.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The header exposes a coherent Theme control with light/dark/system choices, clear selected/focus/hover states, and consistent usable sizing in both themes and responsive layouts. 2. A shared document-action treatment links directly to the generated PDF with a clear neutral label; redundant print behavior is removed or deliberately secondary. 3. The first keyboard focus offers a visible skip link to the shared main content, and repeated header controls remain keyboard accessible. 4. localStorage failures do not prevent page mounting, system mode still responds correctly, and hydration remains warning-free. 5. Controls are centrally styled, hidden from print, covered by focused tests/inspection, and npm run check passes.

title: Optimize article media and navigation speculation
description:
Goal:
Reduce unnecessary page and image work while preserving the article screenshots' theme-aware presentation and ordinary multi-page navigation.

Relevant approved context:
The Tealab article uses separate 2628×1390 light and dark PNGs of roughly 300 KB each. The shared Image component switches filename variants and sets decoding=async but does not provide intrinsic dimensions, lazy loading, responsive sources, or modern compressed formats. Every HTML entry also requests immediate prerendering of all three other routes, regardless of likely navigation.

Scope:
- Add intrinsic width/height or equivalent aspect-ratio information to article images so static rendering and hydration reserve the correct space.
- Default below-the-fold article media to loading=lazy while preserving an explicit override for any future above-the-fold critical image.
- Produce appropriately sized responsive WebP and/or AVIF assets for both light and dark variants, retaining the existing PNGs only as necessary fallbacks.
- Extend the shared Image/themed-source behavior without exposing arbitrary styling props or requiring custom JSX inside ordinary Markdown.
- Ensure only the effective theme asset is selected, switching themes remains correct, alt text is unchanged, and print output remains useful.
- Remove the current immediate prerender-all-routes rules unless measured evidence justifies them. If speculation is retained, use a conservative interaction-linked prefetch/prerender policy that does not eagerly render every long page on initial load.
- Centralize any entry-head generation so the four HTML files do not retain hand-duplicated speculation rules.
- Update docs/architecture.md to describe the selected media and navigation-loading policy.
- Add observable browser/network or production-output checks for dimensions, lazy behavior, correct theme source, asset existence, and absence of unconditional immediate prerender rules.

Non-goals:
No CDN, image service, JavaScript carousel, visual redesign of screenshots, changed alt copy, page-transition framework, service worker, or speculative preloading without evidence.

Expected validation:
Build and inspect generated image assets and HTML; verify light/dark switching, intrinsic layout, below-fold loading, print presentation, and ordinary navigation at desktop/mobile; finish with npm run check.

Completion criteria:
Article images reserve layout space, load lazily below the fold, use materially smaller responsive theme variants with safe fallback, and still switch correctly; the site no longer immediately prerenders all other pages without evidence; architecture and checks protect the chosen policy; and all validation passes.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: Image/shared UI boundaries, static entry model, responsive behavior, performance enhancement, and validation.
- src/ui/Image.tsx: current theme observation and filename substitution.
- src/components/MarkdownDocument.tsx: Markdown image mapping.
- public/images/articles/tealab/: current light/dark assets.
- index.html and supporting HTML entries: current duplicated immediate speculation rules.
- scripts/check-content-assets.mjs: current themed-variant validation.
- tests/site.e2e.ts: existing themed-image browser test.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Article images have intrinsic dimensions, lazy-load below the fold, and use responsive modern light/dark assets with valid fallback while preserving current alt text. 2. Theme changes select the correct effective image without loading or displaying the wrong variant, and print remains usable. 3. Unconditional immediate prerendering of all other routes is removed; any retained speculation is conservative and evidence-backed. 4. Asset and observable browser/output checks protect the behavior, docs/architecture.md is updated, and npm run check passes.

title: Scaffold the validated application foundation
description:
Goal:
Establish the minimal runnable project and a stable validation baseline for the static single-page React application.

Relevant approved context:
The site uses React, strict TypeScript, Vite, plain CSS, Biome, and Vitest. The production output is static and uses the root GitHub Pages base path. Every npm dependency must use the newest compatible release that is at least seven days old when resolved. Validation should include only checks that are meaningful at this stage and expand in later beads.

Scope:
- Add the package manifest and lockfile, React and Vite entry points, and strict TypeScript configuration.
- Pin a supported Node and npm toolchain that implements the release-age policy.
- Add a root `.npmrc` with `min-release-age=7`, `save-exact=true`, and `engine-strict=true`; do not configure exclusions or override the age gate.
- Resolve every production and development dependency to its newest compatible version eligible under the seven-day gate, pin direct versions exactly, and generate the committed lockfile under that policy.
- Render a deliberately minimal neutral application shell without inventing CV prose.
- Configure Biome and Vitest and provide scripts for formatting and linting, type checking, unit tests when genuine logic exists, and the production build.
- Establish `npm run check` as the stable ordered validation entry point for the checks currently available.
- Produce a static `dist/` build compatible with the root path used by `mikko-finell.github.io`.

Non-goals:
No release-age exemptions, deliberately stale dependency versions, canonical content migration, shared component system, finished visual design, document sections, Playwright suite, GitHub Actions workflow, backend, router, state framework, or styling framework.

Expected validation:
Confirm the project npm configuration reports the seven-day release gate, exact-save behavior, and strict engine enforcement. Run a clean lockfile install and `npm run check`, and confirm the generated production artifact contains only static client files.

Completion criteria:
A fresh lockfile install under the pinned toolchain can reproduce, validate, and build the minimal application; every resolved npm package obeys the seven-day release gate; direct dependencies are exact; and no architecture outside the approved stack is introduced.

References:
- docs/architecture.md: core stack, dependency version policy, source structure, validation contract, static build requirements, and root GitHub Pages base path.
- https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/using-npm/config/: authoritative `min-release-age` behavior and units.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The repository pins a supported Node and npm toolchain and has a root `.npmrc` containing `min-release-age=7`, `save-exact=true`, and `engine-strict=true`, with no release-age exclusions. 2. Every production and development dependency is the newest compatible version eligible under the seven-day gate when resolved; direct dependencies are exact and the committed lockfile was generated under the same policy. 3. The repository has a React, strict TypeScript, and Vite application with a neutral minimal render. 4. Biome, type checking, Vitest, and the production build are exposed through package scripts appropriate to the current scaffold. 5. A clean lockfile install and `npm run check` pass under the pinned toolchain. 6. The production build emits static files in `dist/` using the root Pages base path. 7. No router, state framework, CSS framework, backend, final CV prose, speculative component library, browser suite, or deployment workflow is introduced.
close_reason: Established the pinned React, TypeScript, Vite, Biome, and Vitest foundation; verified the seven-day dependency policy, clean install, validation suite, and root-path static build.
